#+title: Journal event version fixtures (MUST-7 / NS-08)

Per-type event versioning, ratified in =m_1788571429536242416_dca73dd4=: a fixture set
exists before the first real read-time transform. =assignment_prompt_projected= is the one
type whose current version is 2 (it gained the required =artifact_baseline=); every other
type stays at 1. Read mode admits every version up to the current one; append mode requires
the current one; a version beyond the current one is refused as =unsupported_event_version=.
The read-side upgraded view of a version-1 projection carries
={"status": "unrecorded"}= -- an explicit claim that the journal does not know -- and that
shape is never valid on a journal line, in either mode; only the reducer's in-memory view
mode (=:view=) admits it. The chain bytes are never rewritten.

Files named =*.malformed.json= are rejected in both modes.

* Gate types at version 2 (D3, rulings =m_1788583146000=)
=gate_started= v2 adds the required =attempt=, =deadline_unix= and =execution{pid, pgid,
start, claim_hash}=; the view of a v1 line carries =execution {"status": "unrecorded"}= and
no attempt or deadline (an unresolved start). =gate_failed= v2 keeps the integer
=exit_status= for a normal non-zero exit and uses =null= plus a required closed
=termination{kind timeout|signal|recovery, signal only for kind signal, settled, leftovers,
proof}= otherwise; the view of a v1 line carries =termination {"status": "unrecorded"}=.
The stderr evidence union is preserved in both versions: at least one of =stderr_hash= /
=stderr_merged=; v2 admits both together. Fixtures =gate_started.*= and =gate_failed.*=
cover v1 (valid under the current read rules), v2 closed shapes, malformed shapes, and the
future version. The public JSON Schema export is append-only: v2 present, v1 absent.
=gate_v2_positive.jsonl= supplies the version-2 positive samples the contract suite draws
from (the archived parity journals keep their version-1 gate lines byte-identical; the
reducer starts emitting version 2 only in the wiring unit).
